title: Reclaiming Media Leadership in the Streaming Era: Strategic Capabilities and Transformation Pathways of Warner Bros. Discovery
summary: The shift from scheduled, channel-based distribution to on-demand, consumer-centric streaming has forced legacy media conglomerates to reconfigure their content libraries, brand assets, and monetization models simultaneously. This study takes Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) as a revelatory case of legacy-media transformation. The analysis shows that WBD has unique advantages, namely, a highly diversified intellectual property portfolio, a high-quality brand equity of HBO, cross-platform promotion synergy, and a gradually improved monetization mode of mixed streaming media. However, the company's transformation is severely limited by the following factors: brand dilution caused by chaotic content integration, mismatch of time and cash flow between linear TV revenue decline and large-scale streaming media expenditure, heavy debt burden after merger and acquisition, and highly unstable distribution window strategy. In order to overcome the above systematic problems, this paper gives a set of operable solutions, namely, re-establishing obvious brand differences, implementing cross-cycle capital allocation, giving priority to positive deleveraging, and maintaining the company's windowing rules. The findings suggest that sustainable media leadership rests less on catalog scale alone than on an organization's capacity to coordinate and monetize heterogeneous cross-platform assets under financial discipline. This study gives a very critical strategic framework for understanding the digital transformation that diversified traditional media groups are experiencing.

title: How Different Types of Artificial Intelligence Training Relate to Innovative Behavior Among Logistics Employees: A Cognitive–Affective Pathway Model
summary: Despite substantial investments in artificial intelligence (AI) training, logistics organizations often struggle to translate these investments into measurable improvements in employee performance. Drawing on the extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Cognitive Load Theory, and Distributed Cognition Theory, this study examines how three AI-TPACK training dimensions—Strategic, Generative, and Optimization AI Training—are associated with employees’ innovative behavior through cognitive (Task–Technology Fit, AI Self-Efficacy) and affective (Perceived Technology Attractiveness, AI Usage Intention) mechanisms. Survey data from 245 logistics practitioners (cross-sectional, single-source) were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis, competing structural models, and bootstrapped indirect effects in a final integrated model. The originally proposed dual-track structure was not supported; the data favored a cross-linked specification in which cognitive beliefs inform attitudes across tracks and attractiveness precedes usage intention. Strategic AI training was associated with innovative behavior indirectly, Generative AI training both directly and indirectly, and Optimization AI training showed no unique association once the other dimensions were controlled. Neither Training Environment Quality nor Supervisor Support Leadership moderated the hypothesized relationships in a robust way, although both showed direct associations with outcomes (Training Environment Quality with Task–Technology Fit, β = 0.288; Supervisor Support with innovative behavior, β = 0.141). These cross-sectional, single-source associations refine the technology acceptance literature for AI training and inform HRD strategies for digital transformation in logistics.

title: Data-Driven Decision Making in Banking via Real-Time Reporting Systems
summary: The banking sector is undergoing a rapid digital transformation fueled by technological innovation, regulatory shifts, and changing customer expectations. Among these changes, data-driven decision-making has emerged as a critical enabler of efficiency, competitiveness, and resilience. This manuscript examines the role of real-time reporting systems in supporting data-driven decision-making within banking institutions. By leveraging continuous data streams, advanced analytics, and interactive dashboards, real-time reporting provides banks with instant insights into customer behavior, transaction patterns, fraud detection, credit risk assessment, and operational performance. The study emphasizes how traditional reporting—often delayed and batch-oriented—fails to keep pace with modern banking needs where milliseconds can determine opportunities or losses. Literature on banking analytics, business intelligence (BI), and decision support systems is reviewed to highlight both theoretical foundations and practical applications. A mixed-method approach is proposed, combining case studies of leading banks, statistical analysis of performance improvements, and interviews with industry experts. Results underscore significant advantages, including faster decision cycles, improved compliance reporting, enhanced fraud detection accuracy, and better customer experience. The findings also identify challenges such as data governance, integration complexity, cybersecurity risks, and the need for workforce upskilling. The conclusion advocates for a balanced approach—combining technological infrastructure with regulatory frameworks and organizational culture—to maximize the benefits of real-time reporting. This manuscript contributes to the growing body of research on data-driven banking, offering practical insights for managers, policymakers, and researchers seeking to advance financial decision-making in an era defined by data velocity and complexity.

title: ESG Credibility and Firm Profitability in An Emerging Market: Evidence from ESG Controversies and ESG Gap in Indonesia
summary: ESG is an important channel for a firm's relationship with its stakeholders. The firms are required to not only focus on profit, but they should also consider environmental, social, and governance. This study examines the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance and firm profitability in an emerging market, with a particular emphasis on ESG credibility. Using a balanced panel dataset of 58 firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) over the period 2021–2024 (232 firm-year observations), this study employs ESG data from Refinitiv/LSEG and annual financial statements to measure profitability using Return on Assets (ROA). The empirical model is estimated using fixed-effects panel regression with firm-level clustered robust standard errors. The results indicate that the direct relationship between ESG performance and profitability is not supported in the Indonesian context. However, reputational risk plays a critical role: ESG controversies are significantly associated with profitability, and when operationalized as a high-controversy indicator (Controversy High), this variable exerts a negative effect on ROA. The key finding of this study demonstrates that the ESG Gap (ESG Score − ESGC) has a negative and highly significant impact on ROA, indicating the presence of a credibility penalty when the discrepancy between headline ESG performance and controversy-adjusted ESG scores widens. Robustness tests using an alternative profitability proxy (Net Margin) and alternative ESG measures confirm that the direct effect of ESG on profitability is relatively weak, whereas ESG credibility indicators are more informative. This study contributes to the literature by reinforcing the ESG credibility perspective and providing empirical evidence of reputational penalties and potential greenwashing in emerging markets. title: Data Governance in Financial Reporting Systems: A Study with Voltron Data Mart
summary: Financial reporting systems are critical to ensuring transparency, compliance, and informed decision-making within organizations. However, the accuracy and reliability of these systems depend heavily on robust data governance frameworks that enforce data quality, integrity, security, and accountability. With increasing regulatory demands, enterprises are adopting advanced data platforms such as Voltron Data Mart to enhance governance while enabling scalable analytics. This study examines the role of data governance in financial reporting systems, focusing on the integration and utilization of Voltron Data Mart. By analyzing governance models, industry best practices, and real-world case studies, this research highlights how data governance frameworks mitigate risks, improve reporting efficiency, and ensure compliance with international standards such as IFRS, GAAP, and SOX. The findings reveal that embedding governance controls into Voltron Data Mart not only strengthens auditability but also fosters trust among stakeholders, enabling data-driven financial strategies. Ultimately, this manuscript contributes to both academic discourse and industry practice by offering a structured approach to aligning governance with modern financial data infrastructure.

title: Antecedent Configuration Study of Organizational Resilience under Digital Transformation: Based on fsQCA Method
summary: Digital technologies are continuously embedded in enterprise operations. While organizations improve information processing efficiency, they also face new uncertainties such as technology dependence, resource misallocation, and the superposition of external shocks. To explain the multiple formation paths of organizational resilience in the context of digital transformation, this paper constructs a digital empowerment-organizational adaptation-external collaboration configuration framework, incorporating digital infrastructure, data-driven capabilities, organizational agility, organizational learning capabilities, supply chain collaboration capabilities, and external knowledge acquisition capabilities into a unified analysis. Based on 218 structured simulated enterprise samples, fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis is used to conduct necessary condition, sufficiency configuration, and robustness tests. The results show that none of the six single conditions constitutes a necessary condition for high organizational resilience; high organizational resilience has four equivalent paths: digital agility-driven, learning collaboration-driven, digital-organization dual-wheel drive, and internal and external collaboration-driven, with an overall solution consistency of 0.836 and a coverage of 0.854; the formation of low organizational resilience exhibits significant causal asymmetry. Digital capabilities can only be stably transformed into resilience advantages when matched with organizational responsiveness, learning mechanisms, or external collaboration. This research reveals the complementary and substitutive relationships between digital capabilities, internal organizational capabilities, and external network resources from a configurational perspective, providing an analytical basis for enterprises with different resource endowments to choose resilience enhancement paths.

title: Economic policy uncertainty and corporate ESG rating divergence: evidence from China
summary: How does economic policy uncertainty (EPU) affect corporate ESG rating divergence? This study examines the impact of EPU on corporate ESG rating divergence and its mechanism using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2018 to 2022. We find that EPU reduces corporate ESG rating divergence. The mechanism analysis suggests that EPU reduces divergence in corporate ESG ratings by improving the quality of ESG information disclosure. Further analysis indicates that EPU reduces ESG rating divergence for firms with strong financing constraints but increases it for firms with strong profitability. Furthermore, we found that EPU reduces the social ESG rating divergence of firms to the greatest extent, corporate governance ESG rating divergence to the second greatest extent, and environmental ESG rating divergence to the least extent. This study provides a worthwhile theoretical and practical basis for understanding the changes in corporate ESG rating divergence under economic policy uncertainty.

title: Free Trade Zones, Green Finance Policies, and Corporate Green Transition: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Companies
summary: Against the backdrop of ongoing global green transition and trade liberalization, there remains a lack of sufficient micro-level evidence to determine whether institutional openness can improve corporate environmental performance and long-term sustainable development through the development of green finance. Based on data from Chinese A-share listed companies from 2013 to 2024, this paper utilizes the quasi-natural experiment created by the phased establishment of pilot free trade zones and employs a multi-period difference-in-differences model to examine their impact on corporate green transition and the transmission mechanism of green finance policies. The study found that the establishment of pilot free trade zones has significantly promoted the green transformation of enterprises. An analysis of intermediary effects suggests that green finance policy support may constitute a potential transmission channel; however, since its indicators primarily reflect the intensity of policy activities, they cannot yet directly identify the role of actual financing flows. Further analysis of transmission mechanisms reveals that alleviating enterprises’ financing constraints and attracting long-term institutional investors are key channels for promoting corporate green transition. Additionally, an analysis of spatial effects indicates that the development of pilot free trade zones not only benefits the green transition of enterprises in pilot cities but may also generate positive spillover effects on neighboring cities through cross-regional linkages. This paper reveals the environmental benefits of trade liberalization policies and their financial transmission mechanisms, expands research on the relationship between institutional openness and corporate green behavior, and provides policy insights for emerging economies seeking to balance economic openness, environmental protection, and sustainable development goals. However, as the study sample primarily consists of Chinese listed companies, the cross-national applicability of the findings requires further verification.

title: From Theory to Practice: A Systematic Review of Strategic Approaches to Environmental Sustainability
summary: This chapter focuses on the ‘E’, that is, environmental sustainability to further the discussion on integrating environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles into management practices. Through a systematic literature review (SLR) of peer-reviewed research spanning the past two decades, the chapter identifies and synthesises practical approaches that organisations have adopted to embed environmental sustainability within corporate strategy. This study analysed articles indexed in Scopus and Web of Science (WoS) databases from 2005 to 2025 to explore the alignment of environmental sustainability with corporate strategy. From a total of 281 results generated using keyword search, this study analysed 189 articles. Subsequently, findings were reported using document analysis, keywords analysis and thematic analysis. Following the structured guidelines of the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) framework, the analysis revealed environmental performance metrics, green innovation, circular economy models, and sustainable supply chain management as important strategic themes in environmental sustainability. By integrating environmental sustainability with corporate strategy, this chapter bridges the widely acknowledged gap between theoretical ESG frameworks and their implementation in practice. This chapter concludes with a discussion of emerging trends and research gaps, offering practical implications for managers and policy-makers seeking to embed environmental considerations into strategic decision-making as part of a holistic ESG approach. It serves as a fundamental reference for scholars and practitioners aiming to advance ESG integration through evidence-based environmental strategy.

title: Ingeniería de Consistencia Aplicada (ICA): un marco metodológico transversal para el análisis de consistencia entre realidad, registro y norma
summary: El presente Working Paper introduce la Ingeniería de Consistencia Aplicada (ICA™), un marco metodológico transversal destinado a evaluar de forma neutral, sistemática y estructurada el grado de correlación y consistencia existente entre una realidad observable, sus registros verificables y el marco normativo o técnico aplicable (Modelo RRN: Realidad-Registro-Norma). Frente a los abordajes fragmentarios predominantes en la práctica profesional actual (como la auditoría tradicional, el compliance o los sistemas de calidad), este trabajo formaliza una arquitectura unificada basada en un núcleo metodológico permanente y un mecanismo de extensión modular mediante Perfiles de Dominio, ilustrando su aplicación práctica en controversias de coberturas de salud. Puntos clave del documento: Formalización del modelo tridimensional RRN (Realidad, Registro y Norma). Arquitectura de verificación metodológica y trazabilidad de la evidencia. Análisis comparativo y superación de enfoques analíticos fragmentados. Desarrollo conceptual de perfiles sectoriales y separación entre capas de constatación e interpretación. Nota de propiedad intelectual: El presente documento describe el marco conceptual de la metodología ICA™ y del Sistema Operativo TRIVEP®. Los algoritmos, baremos, fórmulas cuantitativas y motores de ejecución se encuentran resguardados como desarrollo técnico propietario.

title: Transforming HR Workflows: The Impact of Process Automation in Oracle HCM Cloud Implementations
summary: This research paper explores the transformative effects of process automation on Human Resources (HR) workflows, specifically within Oracle Human Capital Management (HCM) Cloud implementations. As organizations continue to embrace digital transformation, automation plays a pivotal role in enhancing the efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of HR operations. The study investigates how Oracle HCM Cloud, a leading cloud-based HR solution, integrates process automation into its core functionalities, including recruitment, payroll, talent management, and employee engagement. By examining a set of case studies from diverse organizations that have implemented Oracle HCM Cloud, this research highlights the operational benefits, challenges, and overall impact on HR departments. Process automation within Oracle HCM Cloud offers significant advantages, such as reducing manual effort, minimizing human error, and streamlining workflows. The automation of repetitive tasks such as employee onboarding, benefits administration, and time tracking allows HR professionals to focus on more strategic activities like talent development and organizational planning. Additionally, Oracle HCM Cloud's integration capabilities enable seamless data flow across various HR functions, ensuring consistency and real-time access to critical information. However, the study also uncovers challenges faced during implementation, including resistance to change, the need for upskilling HR staff, and the complexities of integrating automation with existing legacy systems. Furthermore, the research delves into how organizations measure the success of automation, evaluating performance metrics like processing time reduction, employee satisfaction, and cost savings. In conclusion, the paper asserts that while process automation in Oracle HCM Cloud implementations brings substantial improvements to HR workflows, its successful integration requires careful planning, proper change management strategies, and a commitment to continuous optimization. Future research should focus on the long-term impact of automation on employee experience, as well as the potential for leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning within HCM systems to further enhance automation.

title: Optimization of Pharmacy Supply Chains Using AI and Machine Learning
summary: Pharmacy supply chains are under intensifying pressure to deliver the right medicine, in the right quantity, at the right time—while minimizing costs, preventing expiries, and complying with stringent regulatory and quality standards. Conventional forecasting and replenishment methods often struggle with volatile demand, multi-echelon dynamics (manufacturer–wholesaler–pharmacy), and constraints such as cold-chain integrity and controlled-substance regulations. This manuscript presents an integrated framework for optimizing pharmacy supply chains using artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). We synthesize current methods in demand forecasting, inventory control, routing and scheduling, and risk management, and we propose a practical methodology that combines feature-rich forecasting (gradient-boosted trees and sequence models), stochastic inventory optimization, reinforcement learning for adaptive reorder policies, and constraint-aware vehicle routing. A detailed study protocol outlines quasi-experimental deployment across community and hospital pharmacies, including data governance, evaluation metrics, and change-management steps. Illustrative results (based on a realistic implementation scenario) indicate reductions in stockouts (30–50%), expiries (25–40%), and total holding costs (10–20%), with improvements in service level (3–10 percentage points) and forecast accuracy (MAPE reductions from ~22–28% to ~9–14%). We conclude with discussion on interpretability, workforce upskilling, and governance, emphasizing a socio-technical approach that blends human oversight with algorithmic optimization to achieve resilient, ethical, and efficient pharmacy supply chains.

title: Operationalising the impact-finance protocol: institutional architecture and the role of DLT in digital sustainable finance
summary: Sustainable, impact and development finance increasingly rely on digital systems to measure and manage real-world social and environmental performance. Yet impact information is still used primarily for reporting and retrospective assessment, rather than as an operational input into financial decision-making. This creates a persistent gap between what financial systems know about real-world outcomes and how capital is actually allocated, released or constrained. This study examines how that gap might be addressed through the Impact-Finance Protocol (IFP), an institutional architecture designed to connect trusted real-world information with financial execution. Building on the conceptual IFP proposed in earlier work, the study evaluates how the protocol behaves when operationalised under real implementation conditions. A comparative Design Science approach was used, combining an initial reference implementation with a longitudinal programme of implementation across multiple institutional, governance and technical contexts. The protocol, rather than any individual organisation, technology or project, was treated as the unit of analysis. Implementation evidence was systematically reconstructed through evidence validation, qualitative coding, implementation-episode reconstruction, comparative analysis and Design Knowledge synthesis. The findings show that the core responsibilities for structuring evidence and verifying its meaning remain comparatively stable across different implementation contexts. By contrast, connecting verified information to financial action requires more extensive governance, institutional authority and operational coordination than the original architecture anticipated. Practical implementation also depends on cross-cutting capabilities such as legal identity, compliance, financial accounts, payment rails and coordination across recurring and overlapping implementation processes. Community participation emerges as an operational capability, while system-level Assessment remains comparatively immature and requires further implementation and evaluation. Where distributed ledger technology (DLT) mechanisms were used, they supported selective integrity, coordination and governed execution, but remained context-dependent rather than necessary architectural components; off-chain verification, institutional authority and governance remained fundamental to financial activation. The study contributes implementation-derived Design Knowledge and transferable Design Principles for digital sustainable finance. It shows that enabling trusted impact information to influence financial decisions requires not only reliable data and verification, but an institutional architecture capable of governing how information becomes actionable financial value across diverse real-world settings.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Financial Reporting: Transforming Customized Financial Statements, Decision Intelligence, and Assurance Practices
summary: Financial statements are prepared from trial balances that have passed internal-control checks and, for external reporting, have been audited before stakeholders rely on them. Converting this verified ledger into the views needed by investors, creditors, regulators, and management remains largely manual, causing rework, delays, and duplicated reconciliation. This study designs and evaluates an artificial intelligence (AI)-coordinated architecture that generates stakeholder-specific yet reconciled reports from a single governed trial balance. Following a design science approach, the architecture combines centrally configured accounting policies and KPI definitions, lineage metadata, account classification, anomaly detection, sequence forecasting, financial natural language processing (NLP), role-aware customization, and human-in-the-loop explainable AI (XAI). The prototype was evaluated on 15,000 trial balances for 500 entities (12,000 synthetic and 3,000 derived from public SEC filings) against rule-based, robotic process automation (RPA), and commercial generative-AI baselines. It achieved a line-item disclosure fidelity (F1) of 0.965, an AUC of 0.97 for misclassification detection, and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 4.8% for one- to four-quarter forecasts; in 250 simulated multi-entity scenarios, preparer effort fell from 38.0 to 4.2 person-hours per reporting cycle. Simulated stakeholder and auditor responses illustrate the expected gains in perceived usefulness and trust. Limitations include synthetic and statement-derived data, simulated rather than observed perception measures, and an unevaluated narrative-generation module.

title: Corporate Governance Leadership Practices and Reported Company Performance: Evidence from firms Listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: This study examines the relationship between five corporate governance leadership practices and employee-reported company performance in firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange. A cross-sectional survey conducted in 2016 obtained 175 usable responses from nine companies out of 237 questionnaires distributed (73.8%). Reliability assessment, correlation analysis and multiple regression were employed. Each governance dimension was positively correlated with reported performance (r = 0.270–0.369; reported p < 0.001). The joint model explained 18.9% of outcome variation (R² = 0.189; adjusted R² = 0.165; F(5,169) = 7.887, p < 0.001). Leadership composition was the only independently significant predictor (B = 0.214, p = 0.004). These results distinguish simple correlations from independent statistical relationships and highlight the importance of leadership capabilities. The findings concern questionnaire-based performance assessments rather than audited financial returns. Keywords: Corporate governance; leadership composition; leadership independence; stakeholder ownership; ownership concentration; organizational performance; Nairobi Securities Exchange.

title: E-LEADERSHIP, TRUST, DAN KOLABORASI TIM VIRTUAL PADA GENERASI MILENIAL DAN GENERASI Z: SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW DALAM PERSPEKTIF PSIKOLOGI ORGANISASI
summary: Digital transformation has catalyzed the widespread adoption of virtual teams in contemporary organizations, bringing together Millennial and Generation Z workers with distinct behavioral traits. This study aims to systematically analyze literature examining the interrelationships among e-leadership, trust, and virtual team collaboration across generations from an organizational psychology perspective. Adopting the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method guided by PRISMA 2020 protocols, 8 primary studies from reputable databases (2022–2026) were synthesized from an initial pool of 642 identified records. The thematic mapping categorized findings into four core domains: relational competencies of e-leadership, mechanisms of swift trust formation, synchronization of hybrid communication channels, and alignment with supportive-participative leadership expectations for Millennials and Gen Z. Trust consistently serves as a pivotal psychological mediator that mitigates isolation risks and enhances collaborative effectiveness in technology-mediated environments. This review concludes that virtual team performance relies not merely on digital infrastructure, but fundamentally on human-centered, adaptive leadership. ABSTRAK Transformasi digital telah mendorong adopsi tim virtual secara masif dalam organisasi modern, mempertemukan angkatan kerja Generasi Milenial dan Generasi Z yang memiliki karakteristik unik. Kajian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis secara sistematis literatur mengenai keterkaitan e-leadership, trust, dan kolaborasi tim virtual lintas generasi dari sudut pandang psikologi organisasi. Melalui metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) berpedoman PRISMA 2020, sebanyak 8 artikel primer terindeks bereputasi (2022–2026) disintesis dari penelusuran awal 642 dokumen. Hasil pemetaan literatur mengelompokkan temuan ke dalam empat domain utama, yaitu kompetensi relasional e-leadership, mekanisme pembentukan swift trust, integrasi kanal komunikasi hibrida, serta pemenuhan ekspektasi kepemimpinan suportif-partisipatif bagi Generasi Milenial dan Z. Kepercayaan terbukti menjadi mediator psikologis vital yang meminimalkan kerentanan isolasi sosial serta mengoptimalkan kolaborasi tim virtual. Kajian ini menyimpulkan bahwa efektivitas tim virtual tidak hanya bertumpu pada infrastruktur digital, melainkan pada kapasitas kepemimpinan yang adaptif dan berorientasi manusiawi (human-centered).

title: Strategic Positioning and Organizational Performance in Banking Sector: A Case of Equity Bank Rwanda Plc
summary: The purpose of this study was to assess the influence of strategic positioning on organizational performance in the banking sector, with specific reference to Equity Bank Rwanda Plc. Strategic positioning has become a critical determinant of organizational success in the increasingly competitive and technology-driven banking industry. Despite continuous investments in strategic initiatives, many commercial banks in Rwanda continue to face challenges related to operational efficiency, customer retention, service differentiation, and sustainable performance. Limited empirical evidence exists on how specific strategic positioning dimensions, namely cost leadership, product differentiation, and digital positioning, contribute to organizational performance within the Rwandan banking context. The study adopted a cross-sectional survey design using a mixed-methods approach. The target population comprised 109 employees of Equity Bank Rwanda Plc, from which a sample of 86 respondents was selected using Slovin’s formula and stratified sampling techniques. Primary data were collected through structured questionnaires and interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis with SPSS version 30, while qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed a response rate of 98.8%, indicating high reliability of the collected data. Descriptive results showed that cost leadership (M = 4.22), product differentiation (M = 4.21), and digital positioning (M = 4.23) were widely practiced within the bank. Correlation analysis indicated significant positive relationships between cost leadership (r = .747, p < .001), product differentiation (r = .665, p < .001), digital positioning (r = .758, p < .001), and organizational performance. Multiple regression results demonstrated that strategic positioning explained 72.4% (R² = .724) of the variation in organizational performance. Cost leadership (β = .478, p < .001), digital positioning (β = .373, p < .001), and product differentiation (β = .265, p < .001) were all significant predictors of organizational performance. The study concludes that strategic positioning is a critical driver of organizational performance in the banking sector. Cost leadership enhances operational efficiency and profitability, product differentiation strengthens customer loyalty and market competitiveness, while digital positioning promotes innovation and service delivery effectiveness. The study recommends that Equity Bank Rwanda Plc and other commercial banks intensify cost optimization initiatives, enhance customer-focused product innovation, and expand digital transformation investments. Policymakers, particularly the National Bank of Rwanda, should strengthen policies that support digital banking innovation and strategic competitiveness to foster sustainable sector-wide performance. Keywords: Strategic Positioning, Organizational Performance, Cost Leadership, Product Differentiation, Digital Positioning, Banking Sector.

title: Market-Average Data Can Misrepresent Supply Chain Environmental Impacts and Their Uncertainty
summary: Abstract Market-average data sets are often used in life cycle assessment and carbon accounting when the production route of a procured good is unknown. The uncertainty this introduces is commonly characterized using generic pedigree matrix factors, which do not reflect how variability across production geographies and technologies differs between goods. Here, we develop a hybrid method that combines pedigree matrix uncertainty characterization within individual production routes with market-share-weighted Monte Carlo sampling between known production routes to represent uncertainty about which route supplied the good. We compare it with conventional market-average uncertainty analysis for 30 economically important goods. For climate impacts, conventional 5th–95th interpercentile intervals are narrower than route-weighted sampling intervals for 25 goods, at least 50% narrower for 14 goods, and up to 82% narrower. Conventional intervals exclude the central climate impact estimates of 44% of possible production routes. Route-weighted sampling captures these outcomes and reveals multimodality and impact-category-specific uncertainty profiles that conventional analysis does not. Variance decomposition distinguishes geographical and technological differences between routes from uncertainty within routes, helping prioritize supplier data collection. These differences show that conventional uncertainty estimates can mislead and may not capture how substantially initial estimates could change when supplier-specific data become available.

title: Corporate Green Investment and Debt Financing Costs: The Moderating Role of Green Institutional Investor Attention in China
summary: This study examines the association between corporate green investment and subsequent debt financing cost and the moderating role of prior green institutional investor attention. Using 40,060 firm-year observations from 4633 non-financial Chinese A-share firms over investment years 2011–2024, firm and year fixed-effects models relate investment in year t to financing cost in year t + 1, with attention and pre-investment financing cost measured in year t − 1. Green investment is associated with lower subsequent financing cost, and this association becomes more negative as prior attention increases. At the 25th and 75th percentiles of attention, a one-percentage-point increase in green investment relative to total assets is associated with financing-cost reductions of 2.75 and 3.62 basis points, respectively. The negative interaction persists after ownership and selected liability-composition controls, within positive-investment observations, and under alternative clustered and wild-cluster bootstrap inference. Evidence is stronger for financing-cost measures scaled by total liabilities than for the measure based on average core interest-bearing debt. Period comparisons indicate a stronger negative investment association but weaker attention moderation after 2019, including when 2020 is excluded. Differences across firm characteristics and environmental-exposure groups are less conclusive after multiple-testing adjustment. The findings associate the financing relevance of environmental expenditure with prior specialized investor attention, with the strength of the evidence varying across accounting measures and periods.

title: Green finance as a policy transmission channel for low carbon transition in Europe and Africa and the role of capital allocation efficiency and financial development
summary: Abstract Green finance is increasingly used to mobilise capital for low-carbon transition, yet its relationship with renewable-energy outcomes may depend on financial, institutional, and structural conditions that differ across countries. This study examines green finance as a policy transmission channel associated with low-carbon transition in a balanced panel of 25 European and 25 African countries over 2000–2024 (1,250 country-year observations). Low-carbon transition is measured by renewable energy consumption, with renewable electricity output used as an alternative outcome, and capital allocation efficiency, financial development, institutional quality, economic development, and industrial structure are examined alongside green finance. Two-way fixed effects with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, dynamic System GMM, panel threshold regression, and country-grouped XGBoost with SHAP interpretation are employed. Green finance is positively and significantly associated with low-carbon transition in the fixed-effects and System GMM models, in both institutional-quality threshold regimes, and under the alternative outcome. Capital allocation efficiency is positive but insignificant, whereas financial development is positive and significant only in the baseline and dynamic models. Institutional quality conditions the green finance relationship nonlinearly: interaction models indicate positive moderation, but the threshold model shows a smaller green-finance coefficient above the estimated threshold. Economic development and industrial structure are specification-sensitive, and slope-homogeneity tests reveal significant cross-country heterogeneity. Country-grouped XGBoost attains an out-of-fold R² of 0.509, indicating meaningful but incomplete generalisability to unseen countries. Green finance therefore shows the most consistent association with renewable-energy-based transition, supporting context-sensitive sustainable-finance policies across European and African economies. title: HUBUNGAN PERSONAL VALENCE DENGAN READINESS TO CHANGE PADA PELAKU WIRAUSAHA DI KOMUNITAS KOPERASI KOTA PALEMBANG
summary: The development of digital media requires entrepreneurs to change the way they run their businesses, making an individual’s psychological readiness a crucial factor in this adaptation process. This study aims to examine the relationship between personal valence and readiness to change among entrepreneurs who are members of the Palembang City Cooperative Community. The study employed a quantitative correlational approach involving 110 entrepreneurs selected via simple random sampling from a population of 158 community members. Data were collected using the personal valence scale and the readiness to change scale, which were developed based on the frameworks of Armenakis et al. as well as Holt et al., and were then analyzed using the Pearson product-moment correlation technique. The results indicate a significant positive relationship between personal valence and readiness to change, with a correlation coefficient of 0.595 and a significance level of 0.000 (p<0.05). These findings indicate that the higher entrepreneurs’ assessment of the personal benefits of a change, the higher their readiness to face digital transformation. These research results can serve as a basis for the Palembang City Cooperative and SME Agency in designing mentoring programs that support entrepreneurs’ readiness to navigate the digital business ecosystem. ABSTRAK Perkembangan media digital menuntut pelaku wirausaha untuk mengubah cara mereka menjalankan usaha, sehingga kesiapan psikologis individu menjadi faktor penting dalam proses adaptasi tersebut. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui hubungan antara personal valence dan readiness to change pada pelaku wirausaha anggota Komunitas Koperasi Kota Palembang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif korelasional yang melibatkan 110 pelaku wirausaha yang dipilih melalui teknik simple random sampling dari populasi 158 anggota komunitas. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan skala personal valence dan skala readiness to change yang disusun berdasarkan aspek dari Armenakis et al. serta Holt et al., kemudian dianalisis menggunakan teknik korelasi Pearson Product Moment. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan hubungan positif yang signifikan antara personal valence dan readiness to change, dengan koefisien korelasi sebesar 0,595 dan nilai signifikansi 0,000 (p<0,05). Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa semakin tinggi penilaian pelaku wirausaha terhadap manfaat pribadi dari suatu perubahan, semakin tinggi pula kesiapan mereka menghadapi transformasi digital. Hasil penelitian ini dapat menjadi bahan pertimbangan bagi Dinas Koperasi dan UMK Kota Palembang dalam merancang program pendampingan yang mendukung kesiapan pelaku wirausaha menghadapi ekosistem bisnis digital.

title: Blockchain and shareholder voting rights: Corporate governance challenges and regulatory responses
summary: This paper discusses the criminal law regulation protecting blockchain-powered e-voting as an essential means of corporate governance, paying specific attention to shareholders’ involvement. Using qualitative comparative research methods, this study examines the legal regulations of Egypt and the United Arab Emirates, as well as relevant international documents, such as the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime. E-voting became increasingly popular during the COVID-19 pandemic due to its contribution to improved transparency, effectiveness, and accessibility in general meetings. Blockchain ensures greater security, integrity, and authentication, but it is not risk-free; it poses criminal threats to voting, including voter coercion, unauthorized access, data manipulation, and breaches of confidentiality. This paper evaluates the current state of the law addressing these new types of cyber risks and threats in corporate governance. Finally, it differentiates between common corporate crimes and blockchain-related crimes.

title: THE CROSS-BORDER MIGRATION OF CHINA'S DIGITAL GOVERNANCE EXPERIENCE UNDER THE CHINA-ASEAN DIGITAL ECONOMY COOPERATION FRAMEWORK
summary: With the rapid development of digital technology, digital governance has become an important path to modernizing national governance and a key issue in global economic cooperation. Within the framework of China-ASEAN digital economy cooperation, regional cooperation practices centered on the "Digital Silk Road" have provided fertile ground for the cross-border transfer of China's digital governance experience. This paper, from the dialectical perspective of "development empowerment and sovereignty balance," systematically examines the core elements, current status, and pathways of the cross-border transfer of China's digital governance experience. The study finds that China's digital governance model, characterized by state-capacity leadership, infrastructure exports as a precursor, the promotion of technical standards as a link, and multi-party collaborative governance as a mechanism, has generated significant spillover effects in ASEAN's digital transformation process. This cooperation not only provides ASEAN countries with a development path different from the West and innovates the South-South digital cooperation paradigm, but also injects new momentum into the equitable and diversified transformation of the global digital governance system, highlighting the global governance significance of the "Chinese solution."

title: Calculation of carbon footprint of forestry tourism and optimization of emission reduction strategies in sustainable supply chain management
summary: This study aims to construct a high-precision and dynamic carbon footprint accounting model and provide feasible emission reduction strategy combinations to address specific issues in the forest tourism supply chain, such as blurred boundaries in carbon footprint accounting, static lag in emission factors, and divergent emission reduction strategies in balancing environmental, economic, and social benefits. Firstly, this paper determines the lifecycle accounting boundaries based on the ISO 14067 (International Organization for Standardization) standard, covering upstream material supply, midstream scenic area operation, downstream waste disposal, and tourist return. Then, this paper collects and preprocesses multi-source heterogeneous data, including smart meter data and GPS (Global Positioning System) trajectories, to address data silos and noise issues. Next, this paper introduces a triple dynamic correction mechanism based on load factors, grid time series marginal emission factors, and biodynamic parameters to achieve spatiotemporal dynamic perception of carbon footprint. Also, this paper takes the dynamic accounting results as input and constructs a multi-objective optimization model with clean energy substitution rate as the decision variable. Finally, this paper uses NSGA-II (Non dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II) and elite strategy to solve the Pareto front, achieving closed-loop collaboration between accounting accuracy and multi-dimensional objective trading operations. The experimental results show that the average absolute percentage error of the carbon footprint time series prediction method in this paper is 2.01%; the unit emission reduction cost is 40.97 yuan/ton of carbon dioxide equivalent; the tourist satisfaction index reaches 0.87. The method proposed in this paper combines triple dynamic factor correction with three-dimensional NSGA-II multi-objective optimization, significantly improving the accuracy of carbon footprint calculation in the forestry tourism supply chain, and formulating emission reduction strategies that consider environmental, economic, and social benefits.

title: KAP Reputation, Audit Fee, Audit Tenure, and Audit Quality of IDX-Listed Companies
summary: Background: Audit quality forms the foundation of the credibility and transparency of corporate financial statements, yet the recurrence of restatements and of sanctions against public accounting firms (KAP) in Indonesia shows that it remains a persistent issue. Objective: This study examines how KAP reputation, audit fee, and audit tenure relate to the audit quality of firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) over 2021–2025. Methods: A quantitative associative design was applied to secondary panel data drawn from audited annual financial statements. Purposive sampling produced 119 listed firms and 595 firm-year observations. The data were examined through binary logistic regression in EViews 12. Results: The binary logistic regression on 595 firm-year observations indicates that KAP reputation significantly lowers the probability of restatement (coefficient −0.9063; p = 0.0268), consistent with higher audit quality, whereas audit fee significantly raises it (coefficient +0.9152; p < 0.001), implying that larger fees accompany a greater likelihood of restatement. Audit tenure is not significant (coefficient −0.1809; p = 0.2025). The McFadden R² of 0.6706 reflects a substantial improvement in fit over the null model, and the Hosmer–Lemeshow test (p = 0.1194) points to adequate goodness of fit. Conclusion: Firms audited by internationally affiliated (Big Ten) KAP show a lower likelihood of restatement, signaling higher audit quality, whereas higher fees accompany a greater likelihood of restatement a direction in line with the economic-bonding perspective while audit tenure does not determine audit quality.

title: The In-Depth Challenges and Opportunities of Enterprise Digital Transformation
summary: In the digital era, digital transformation can be regarded as a "reconstruction of the underlying architecture" of an enterprise's management system. With the increasing maturity of technologies such as big data, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things, traditional product and service models have struggled to form effective competitiveness. As a result, digital transformation has evolved from an "optional choice" to a "mandatory requirement" critical to the survival of enterprises. In the process of transformation, enterprises are faced with challenges not only at the technical level, but also in the overall upgrading of skill structure and organizational capability from the management level to each business department. This paper systematically analyzes the common problems in the digital transformation of enterprises, puts forward corresponding solutions, and discusses the internal mechanism of digital transformation to promote the long-term development of enterprises.

title: Green Credit Policy and Financing Costs in China's New Energy Vehicle Supply Chain
summary: Against the backdrop of China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, green credit has become an important policy instrument for directing financial resources toward low-carbon industries. This study examines financing-cost patterns among 15 Chinese A-share listed firms in the new energy vehicle (NEV) supply chain from 2015 to 2022. Using 115 firm-year observations, the analysis combines descriptive statistics, period comparison, pooled OLS regression, and two-way fixed-effects estimation. The results show that average financing costs are lower in 2019-2022 than in 2015-2018, but the difference is not statistically significant. In the pooled OLS model, firm size is negatively associated with financing cost, whereas the later-period indicators, profitability, and debt-to-equity ratio, are statistically insignificant. After controlling for firm and year fixed effects, the association between firm size and financing cost weakens substantially, and none of the examined firm characteristics remains statistically significant. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for firm heterogeneity and time effects when examining financing-cost patterns in China's NEV supply chain.

title: Digital Transformation in Village Financial Governance: A Case Study of Village Financial System Implementation in Rural Indonesia
summary: Digital financial governance has become increasingly important in strengthening administrative accountability and financial management practices at the village level. However, the implementation of digital financial systems in rural administrations remains constrained by infrastructural limitations and varying levels of institutional capacity. This study explores the implementation of the Village Financial System (SISKEUDES) in Lempang Village, Barru Regency, Indonesia, with particular attention to its administrative functions and the challenges encountered by village officials. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, data were collected through direct observation, semi-structured interviews with purposively selected village officials, and document analysis. The findings reveal that SISKEUDES facilitates the integration of financial planning, transaction recording, financial reporting, and document management within a more structured administrative process. Its implementation supports the organization and traceability of financial records, although the available evidence does not establish measurable improvements in operational efficiency or public financial transparency. Two major challenges emerged: unreliable internet connectivity, which disrupts data processing, and disparities in officials' technical competencies, which influence the consistency of system utilization. These findings highlight the interdependence of technological infrastructure, human resource capacity, and administrative practices in implementing digital financial governance at the village level. The study contributes contextual evidence to discussions of digital governance in rural public administration, emphasizing that technological adoption alone is insufficient to ensure effective financial management without adequate institutional and infrastructural support.

title: Economic Interpretation of the Distorting Effects of High Inflation on Financial Reporting and the Case of Türkiye
summary: Abstract This study examines the effects of high inflation on financial reporting through a framework linking accounting measurement to economic decisions. It uses a purposive narrative review of Turkish and English literature, IAS 29, and Turkish Accounting Standard TMS 29, together with theoretical analysis. The framework distinguishes three sources of distortion: the aggregation of amounts expressed in purchasing power from different dates, divergence between the general price level and firm-specific prices, and incomplete interpretation of the wealth effects of monetary exposure. These distinctions imply that nominal profit growth cannot be equated with improved real performance and that inflation adjustments need not affect all firms in the same direction. The study contributes conditional propositions connecting measurement problems to dividend distribution, investment, credit assessment, and capital allocation. A hypothetical numerical illustration demonstrates that maintaining general purchasing power and maintaining physical productive capacity can yield different assessments of distributable surplus. Inflation accounting supports comparability but cannot fully eliminate relative-price changes, liquidity risk, or uncertainty about future cash flows. Accordingly, financial statements in high-inflation environments should be interpreted jointly with monetary exposure, asset age, the working-capital cycle, and the concept of capital maintenance. The propositions are theoretical expectations for future empirical testing rather than estimated causal effects. Keywords: high inflation, financial reporting, inflation accounting, monetary exposure, capital maintenance

title: Post-harvest stages account for more than half of seafood carbon footprint
summary: Abstract Seafood is increasingly important for healthy dietary transitions in modern urban lifestyles. Yet, the patterns of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions remain poorly understood, which hinders the low-carbon pathways for city-specific seafood supply chains. Here, we constructed a disaggregated supply chain dataset to quantify the GHG footprint of consumption of five major seafood categories across 313 Chinese cities. In 2023, total GHG footprint of Chinese seafood consumption reached 182.6 Mt CO₂-eq (1.5% of the national total emissions), dominated by shellfish (65.7%) and fish (25.1%). Annual per-capita emissions varied from over 1000 kg CO₂-eq/capita in coastal and tourism cities to near zero in many inland cities. Spatially, 79.9% of emissions were concentrated in coastal cities, with the top five cities contributing 27.2%. Most transported seafood (58–88%) was within 200 km, indicating shorter food miles than other food categories. We find that off-farm supply chain stages, which account for 55% of total emissions, are key to retaining seafood's low-carbon advantage over terrestrial protein sources such as chicken and pork. We highlight the need for coordinated strategies to support both sustainable and healthy diets, including efficient mariculture practices in coastal cities and low-carbon cold-chain logistics and feed production in the supply chain.

title: From Visibility to Recovery: Technology-Enabled Accounting and Accountability for Biodiversity, Species Protection and Ecological Restoration
summary: Biodiversity loss is emerging as a material governance and accountability concern, yet biodiversity reporting often remains fragmented from species protection and ecological recovery. This paper reviews the development of accounting and accountability for biodiversity protection and examines how emerging technologies can reshape biodiversity measurement, corporate governance disclosure and CSR accountability. Drawing on a literature review informed by structured searching, the paper identifies three generations of biodiversity accounting: accounting of biodiversity, focused on measurement and disclosure; accounting for biodiversity and species, focused on responsibility and non-human visibility; and accounting for biodiversity recovery, focused on intervention, restoration and rewilding. The review argues that artificial intelligence, big data analytics, blockchain, and digital platforms can strengthen the visibility, timeliness, traceability and assurance of biodiversity information, but can also introduce new risks of opacity, algorithmic bias, data fragmentation and technology-enabled greenwashing. We develop a technology-enabled accountability framework that links visibility, verification, responsibility, intervention, and recovery. The paper contributes to the emerging literature on technology-enabled corporate governance disclosure and CSR by showing how digital infrastructures can move biodiversity accounting beyond narrative disclosure towards more verifiable and outcome-oriented accountability.

title: A supply chain life cycle framework using social exchange theory
summary: Purpose The purpose of this research is to develop supply chain life cycle theory using the concepts of supply chain uncertainty, supply chain orientation and social exchange theory. Design/methodology/approach This research employs conceptual research methodology to develop theoretical propositions of the relationships that are fundamental to supply chain processes, while following established theory-building guidelines in supply chain management. Findings Supply chain processes must be examined longitudinally, sequentially and as multiple cycles of events and conditions of multiple firms. Doing so can provide theoretical insights into the birth, continuance and dissolution of supply chains. Originality/value This research offers a temporal, process explanation of how supply chain uncertainty may generate supply chain orientation and supply chain management responses, how those responses subsequently alter uncertainty and how this recursive process may help explain the emergence, continuation, adaptation and dissolution of SCM activities and supply chains.
